B6.1.done: 4 candidates built by e5lib.factory from the s04 recipes.json (one spec per family) with the s06 settings from protocol.yaml; every pipeline fitted inside each of the 5 training folds (137,255 training rows over the folds). Learned imputation values per fold are in imputation_by_fold.csv, with the validation rows whose category level was unseen in the training fold (the one-hot step encodes them as all zeros).
B6.1.inputs: s04 recipes.json and selected_features.json; s05 folds.csv; s02 records (development rows).
B6.1.label: observation

B6.2.done: Families basic to complex, validation mae mean ± SE over the folds: dummy 5.9689 ± 0.7107 days; linear/logistic 5.0247 ± 0.6115 days; single tree 5.0532 ± 0.6394 days; forest 4.9627 ± 0.6457 days. Ladder: linear/logistic kept over dummy; single tree not kept over linear/logistic; forest not kept over linear/logistic. One-SE choice over all four: linear/logistic (best mean: forest).
B6.2.observation: Paired per-fold gain of each step (positive = the more complex family is better; description only, s01 1.7): linear/logistic vs dummy +0.9442 days (paired SE 0.1606), better in 5 of 5 folds; single tree vs linear/logistic -0.0285 days (paired SE 0.1027), better in 2 of 5 folds; forest vs linear/logistic +0.0619 days (paired SE 0.0677), better in 3 of 5 folds.
B6.2.reasoning: A more complex family is adopted only when its gain over the current family clears one standard error of the fold means (the agreed rule). The fold SE also carries the level differences between folds (drift), so a small but consistent paired gain can stay below it; the paired figures show that without changing the decision.
B6.2.conclusion: These are selection scores on the folds, not generalisation estimates (G-10). s07 tunes the linear and tree families and compares each tuned configuration with its plain s06 model (G-55).
B6.2.label: observation
